decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r3 report 0.94 versus 1.08 TFLOPs per image, making Sablewing about 13% lower; “slightly lower” is a calibrated description of that difference.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r3 report 3.9 versus 4.5 seconds per batch, making Sablewing about 13% faster; “slightly lower” is calibrated to the reported values.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r3 report FID 7.8 versus 15.6; Sablewing’s value is exactly half, adequately supporting “much lower.”

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 8 versus 50 NFE on Halvern-Faces 256×256, a more than sixfold reduction that supports the characterization “markedly more efficient.”

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 0.94 versus 5.40 TFLOPs per image, nearly a sixfold reduction that supports “markedly more efficient” in computational cost.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 3.9 versus 21.7 seconds per batch of 64 under the same timing setup, over a fivefold reduction supporting “markedly more efficient.”

decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 establish the efficiency–FID tradeoff only for Halvern-Faces. Stating it for 256×256 face generation generally exceeds the demonstrated dataset scope.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 show large reductions across all three cost measures while FID rises only from 7.1 to 7.8; “modest” is a calibrated descriptive characterization, not a significance claim.
